entries.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: one single photorealistic rehabilitation step demonstration photograph, 168 T-AXU-030 s01, portrait 4:5, output approximately 1122 x 1402 pixels.
Input images: Image 1 (168_T-AXU-030_s02.png) is the EDIT TARGET and exact invariant composition/equipment/environment/body-position source. Images 2, 3, 4 (reference-01.png, reference-02.png, reference-03.png) are supporting IDENTITY REFERENCES for the same adult Asian woman, facial identity, hair, build and clothing. Do not reproduce the reference arm poses.
Primary request: edit ONLY both arms and both matching light grey dumbbells from the overhead finish position to the shoulder-level starting position of a seated shoulder press.
Exact new posture: remain seated firmly on the identical stable upholstered grey backrest chair, identical feet flat on the ground, hips and pelvis and torso in the same position, back upright supported near the chair back, no lumbar arch, chest natural. Both hands hold the same two light grey dumbbells beside her shoulders at about ear/shoulder height; elbows bent approximately 90 degrees, located comfortably forward-outside the torso rather than spread far backward; forearms close to vertical, wrists natural/neutral, secure anatomically correct closed grips. The dumbbells are held slightly anterior to the shoulder line and are not resting on her shoulders. This is a clean static starting frame.
Invariants: lock the exact camera, perspective, figure scale, chair location/design, lighting, grey-blue seamless background and floor, face, ponytail, white short-sleeve T-shirt, charcoal trousers, white sneakers, sitting position, leg/foot position from image 1. The frame must remain the same portrait 4:5 full body image. Keep all hands, elbows, dumbbells, chair legs and both shoes within the canvas.
Style: realistic medical exercise instructional studio photography with natural anatomy and soft even light.
Avoid: standing, empty hands, a second person, extra hands/fingers/limbs, floating dumbbells, joint deformities, motion blur, exercise machines, labels, numbers, text, watermarks, arrows, collage, split panels. Produce exactly ONE single image.

entries.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: one single photorealistic rehabilitation step demonstration photograph, 169 T-AXU-031 s01, portrait 4:5 approximately 1122 x 1402 pixels.
Input images: Image 1 (169_T-AXU-031_s02.png) is the EDIT TARGET and exact invariant composition/environment/equipment source. Images 2, 3, 4 (reference-01.png, reference-02.png, reference-03.png) are supporting IDENTITY REFERENCES locking the same adult Asian woman's face, ponytail, build and white short sleeve T-shirt/charcoal trousers.
Primary request: edit ONLY the woman's two arm/hand positions and the corresponding grey elastic resistance tubes to depict the STARTING raised-arm position of a seated front lat pulldown. Keep all other pixels/composition as invariant as possible.
Exact new posture: seated securely at the identical location on the identical stable grey chair, hips, knees and both feet identical, both soles flat on the floor, torso upright, neutral head looking forward. Raise both arms forward and upward from her upper chest toward the visible high anchor into a comfortable starting overhead/upper-front position. Hands remain securely gripping the SAME TWO triangular black handles, about 25 to 35 cm above head height and just forward of the forehead, shoulders relaxed, elbows slightly bent rather than locked, wrists neutral, comfortable shoulder-width grip. This is the top/starting frame before bending elbows to bring the handles down toward the upper chest.
Equipment requirements: preserve the exact steel stand and its complete high strap/carabiner anchor, upper beam, vertical upright, and floor base. Both elastic grey resistance tubes must connect logically and directly from the SAME reliable high anchor to their own SAME handles, with shorter visible lengths and mild pre-tension appropriate to the starting pose. The tubes run in FRONT of her body/face plane and never behind her neck; do not replace the tubes with ropes, chains or a bar. The two hands and handles should be clearly separated rather than overlapping each other or the anchor.
Invariants: preserve camera angle and perspective, woman scale and identity, face/hair, clothes/shoes, exact chair position/design, leg and foot positions, steel stand position and design, blue-grey seamless studio background and floor, soft even lighting. Keep full figure, both hands, both handles, high anchor, complete stand and both shoes inside the same 4:5 canvas.
Avoid: posterior-neck pulldown, leaning backward, standing, shrugging, forceful terminal shoulder elevation, broken or disconnected tubing, floating handles, extra limbs/fingers, distorted hands, text, numbers, labels, arrows, watermark, collage, split panels. Produce exactly ONE single photograph.
